comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C115, C117. Both evaluations support the temporal consistency of the scattering number optimization across different sampling periods, strengthening the evolutionary interpretation.
Perfect agreement on claims C155, C156. Both evaluations support the mechanistic insight that collisions with obstacles decorrelate swimming direction from magnetic field alignment.

Both address claims C159, C161, C163. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature of evolutionary predictions, while peer reviewers SUPPORT the evolutionary interpretation and proposed experimental tests without challenge.

Strong agreement on experimental methods (C172-C179). Both evaluations support the methodological approaches, with peer reviewers specifically praising the obstacle array design and controlled bacterial release mechanism.

Strong agreement on core experimental observations (C59-C65). Both evaluations support the qualitative behavior at different field strengths shown in Figure 1 and Video 1, with peer reviewers calling it 'very convincing' and 'beautiful.'

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C148-C153). Both evaluations support the synthesis of experimental, simulation, and comparative data, with peer reviewers affirming the convincing evidence for optimization.

Both address experimental design justification (C48-C58). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculation about natural sediment conditions and acknowledged overrepresentation of convex traps. Peer Reviewer 1 raises similar concerns about convex trap geometry and generalizability to natural environments.

Strong agreement on study organism justification (C37-C43). Both evaluations support the choice of MMB and experimental system, with peer reviewers explicitly endorsing the methodological choices despite limitations of non-culturable organisms.

Agreement on direct measurements (C106-C112). Both evaluations support the observations and accept the authors' acknowledgment that theory cannot explain distribution tail. Peer reviewers note all issues were addressed productively.

Both address comparative analysis across species (C118-C126 overlap). OpenEval supports the consistency of scattering number despite phenotypic variation. Peer reviewers specifically appreciate the cross-species comparisons and statistical analysis (C127, C133-C137 also in peer R4).

Both address theoretical framework (C87, C93, C99 overlap, plus C24 in peer R1). OpenEval supports the dimensional analysis and scattering number predictions. Peer reviewers affirm the model 'convincingly rationalizes' observations with 'good agreement' between experiments and simulations.

Partial overlap on theoretical simplifications (C83). OpenEval supports the justified neglect of rotational diffusion based on dimensional analysis. Peer reviewers support the overall theoretical framework without specifically challenging this simplification.

Partial overlap on statistical testing (C127, C133, C134). OpenEval supports the bootstrapping approach and conclusion about natural selection. Peer reviewers support the overall comparative analysis and optimization evidence without specifically discussing the statistical methodology.

Partial overlap on predicted correlations (C136, C137). OpenEval supports the confirmed correlation in Figure 3b. Peer reviewers appreciate the cross-species analysis broadly but do not specifically address this correlation.

Both address speculative explanations for outliers (C113, C114). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct evidence. Peer reviewers accept these as plausible hypotheses without challenge, noting transparent acknowledgment of limitations.

Minimal overlap (C99). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to assumptions about unreported grain sizes in literature. Peer reviewers support the theoretical framework overall without specifically addressing this uncertainty.
